page: Amazon Web Services r7g.2xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped directly to 8 physical cores powered by the 64-bit ARMv8 AWS Graviton3 Neoverse-V1 processor clocked at 2.6 GHz. The processor includes 64 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache per core cluster. Configured with 64.0 GB of system memory, the instance delivers a generous 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio (8.0 GB per vCPU). Networking features a baseline speed of 4 Gbps, while dedicated GPUs and local NVMe storage are omitted from this configuration.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong memory throughput alongside stable compute capability. In memory subsystem testing, the r7g.2xlarge achieved a PassMark memory score in the top 25% (2959.48), backed by uncached read memory bandwidth of 184.3 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 68.94 GB/sec. General multi-core processing delivers average-tier results with a Geekbench multi-core score of 8171.0 and stress-ng multi-core metric of 12242.92. Cache-sensitive compile tasks executed well, with Geekbench Clang compiling hitting 11839.0.

Hardware tradeoffs emerge under certain compute-heavy workloads. PassMark overall CPU scoring placed in the lower 25% (6073.06), driven down by subdued results in encryption and vector processing tests, partly due to the absence of x86-specific AVX extensions. Similarly, small-model LLM generation runs in the bottom 10% (40.6 tokens/sec). Conversely, the dedicated Arm architecture delivers notable power and resource efficiency per gigabyte of memory compared to older generation x86 equivalents.

Given its high RAM allocation and robust memory bandwidth, the r7g.2xlarge is targeted at in-memory caches, distributed key-value stores like Redis (measured at 13.53 million operations per second), relational database operations, and high-throughput static web serving.
description: Amazon Web Services r7g.2xlarge is an ARM-based memory-optimized instance powered by the 2.6 GHz AWS Graviton3 Neoverse-V1 processor. Operating on the Nitro hypervisor, it supplies 8 dedicated physical cores with a 1:1 core-to-thread ratio, 64.0 GB of system RAM, and a 4 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance does not bundle local disk storage or hardware accelerators. Benchmark evaluations place memory performance within the top tier, scoring 2959.48 in PassMark memory testing and sustaining 184.3 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth. Multithreaded and single-threaded CPU processing hold stable middle-tier metrics across Geekbench and stress-ng, although specialized encryption and LLM text generation metrics reflect lower benchmark percentiles due to x86 vector instruction absence. Thanks to high memory density and efficiency, r7g.2xlarge functions effectively for memory-heavy enterprise workloads, including in-memory databases, Redis deployments, and large caching engines.
